title: 2022 HMMT November Guts Problem 25
statement: In convex quadrilateral \(A B C D\) with \(A B=11\) and \(C D=13\), there is a point \(P\) for which \(\triangle A D P\) and \(\triangle B C P\) are congruent equilateral triangles. Compute the side length of these triangles.

solutions.text: Evidently \(A B C D\) is an isosceles trapezoid with \(P\) as its circumcenter. Now, construct isosceles trapezoid \(A B^{\prime} B C\) (that is, \(B B^{\prime}\) is parallel to \(A C\).) Then \(A B^{\prime} P D\) is a rhombus, so \(\angle B^{\prime} C D=\frac{1}{2} \angle B^{\prime} P D=60^{\circ}\) by the inscribed angle theorem. Also, \(B^{\prime} C=11\) because the quadrilateral \(B^{\prime} A P C\) is a \(60^{\circ}\) rotation of \(A D P B\) about \(P\). Since \(C D=13\), we use the law of cosines to get that \(B^{\prime} D=7 \sqrt{3}\). Hence \(A P=7\).
